# Guard Rules Reference

77 built-in rules that block or warn on dangerous operations.
These evaluate on every PreToolUse event (before tool execution).

## Cloud Providers

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-aws-destructive` | critical | block | AWS destructive operations are not allowed from agent sessions Ask the user to run this manually |
| `builtin-aws-s3-recursive` | high | block | Recursive S3 operations can destroy large amounts of data Ask the user before running recursive S3 operations |
| `builtin-rsync-delete` | high | block | rsync --delete can wipe files at the destination Use rsync without --delete, or ask the user |
| `builtin-gcloud-destructive` | critical | block | GCP destructive operations are not allowed from agent sessions Ask the user to run this manually |
| `builtin-az-destructive` | critical | block | Azure destructive operations are not allowed from agent sessions Ask the user to run this manually |

## Containers

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-docker-prune` | high | block | docker prune removes potentially important data Ask the user before pruning Docker resources |
| `builtin-compose-down-v` | high | block | docker-compose down -v removes volumes (data loss) Use 'down' without -v to preserve data volumes |
| `builtin-kubectl-mass-delete` | critical | block | kubectl mass deletion is not allowed Delete specific resources instead |
| `builtin-kubectl-drain` | high | block | kubectl drain evicts all pods from a node Ask the user before draining nodes |
| `builtin-helm-uninstall` | high | block | helm uninstall/delete removes Kubernetes releases and their resources Ask the user to run this manually |
| `builtin-docker-rm-force` | high | block | docker rm -f kills running containers without graceful shutdown Use docker stop first, then docker rm |
| `builtin-docker-volume-rm` | high | block | docker volume rm destroys persistent data in named volumes Ask the user before removing Docker volumes |
| `builtin-kubectl-delete-all` | critical | block | kubectl delete --all mass-deletes Kubernetes resources Delete specific resources instead |

## Database

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-drop-database` | critical | block | Database/table/schema destruction is irreversible Verify target and create a backup first |
| `builtin-truncate-table` | critical | block | TRUNCATE TABLE deletes all data irrecoverably Verify table name and use transaction |
| `builtin-delete-no-where` | high | block | DELETE without WHERE clause removes all rows Add a WHERE clause to target specific rows |
| `builtin-mongodb-drop` | critical | block | MongoDB drop operations are irreversible Ask the user before dropping MongoDB collections |
| `builtin-redis-flush` | critical | block | Redis FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB clears all data Ask the user before flushing Redis |

## File Deletion

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-rm-rf-root` | critical | block | Recursive deletion of root-level or wildcard paths is dangerous Be more specific about what to delete |
| `builtin-rm-wrangler` | critical | block | CRITICAL: .wrangler contains the local development database (SQLite). Deleting it DESTROYS ALL LOCAL DATA. To fix deployment issues, try: rm -rf .wrangler/cache (keeps database) |
| `builtin-rm-node-modules` | medium | block | Deleting node_modules requires a full reinstall If you have dependency issues, try: npm cache clean --force && npm install |

## Filesystem

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-dd-block-device` | critical | block | Writing directly to block devices with dd can destroy data Verify the target device carefully |
| `builtin-disk-format` | critical | block | Disk formatting/partitioning commands are not allowed Ask the user to run this manually |
| `builtin-shred` | critical | block | shred securely overwrites files making recovery impossible Use rm for normal deletion |
| `builtin-wipefs` | critical | block | wipefs erases filesystem signatures from block devices Ask the user to run this manually |

## Git Operations

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-git-force-push` | critical | block | git push --force can destroy remote commits and collaborators' work Use --force-with-lease for safer force pushing |
| `builtin-git-reset-hard` | high | block | git reset --hard destroys all uncommitted changes Use git stash first to preserve changes |
| `builtin-git-clean-f` | high | block | git clean -f permanently deletes untracked files Use git clean -n first to preview what will be deleted |
| `builtin-git-checkout-dot` | high | block | git checkout -- . discards all unstaged changes Use git stash first to preserve changes |
| `builtin-git-restore-worktree` | high | block | git restore --worktree discards working tree changes Use git stash first to preserve changes |
| `builtin-git-branch-D` | medium | block | git branch -D force-deletes a branch without merge check Use -d instead for safe deletion |
| `builtin-git-stash-destroy` | high | block | git stash drop/clear permanently removes stashed work Verify stash contents first with git stash list |
| `builtin-git-filter-branch` | critical | block | git filter-branch/filter-repo rewrites entire repository history This is a destructive rewrite of all commits. Ask the user to run manually |
| `builtin-git-restore-dot` | high | block | git restore . discards all unstaged changes Use git stash first to preserve changes, or restore specific files |

## Process Killing

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-pkill-f` | high | block | pkill -f matches processes across ALL projects/sessions Use specific PID: kill <pid>. To kill local dev processes, be specific: pkill -f 'wrangler dev' |
| `builtin-killall` | high | block | killall terminates ALL processes with matching name Use specific PID: kill <pid> |
| `builtin-pkill-node` | high | block | Would kill processes across all projects Use specific PID or port-based killing: lsof -ti :<port> | xargs kill. To kill local dev processes, be specific: pkill -f 'wrangler dev' |
| `builtin-pgrep-xargs-kill` | high | block | Pattern kills processes system-wide Use specific PID or port-based killing |
| `builtin-kill-signal` | high | block | Sending termination signals is dangerous. Use plain 'kill <PID>' (SIGTERM) instead Use plain: kill <PID> |
| `builtin-kill-multi-pid` | high | block | Killing multiple PIDs at once is dangerous Kill one PID at a time |
| `builtin-kill-substitution` | high | block | kill with command substitution or piped xargs is dangerous Find the PID first, then kill it by number |
| `builtin-pkill-signal` | high | block | pkill with signal kills matching processes system-wide Use specific PID: kill -<signal> <pid> |
| `builtin-kill-port` | medium | soft_block | This will kill a process listening on a port (possibly a dev server). If you need to restart the server, re-run this command. Confirm this is intentional — a running dev server may be in use by the user or another agent |

## Process Safety

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-fork-bomb` | critical | block | Fork bomb detected — this will exhaust system resources and freeze the machine Do not run fork bombs. If you need parallel processes, use controlled concurrency |
| `builtin-nohup-network` | critical | block | Detached background process with network capability — this is a RAT persistence pattern (ref: axios@1.14.1 used nohup python3 dropper with ppid:1) Run network commands in the foreground so their output is visible and they terminate with the session |
| `builtin-background-network` | high | warn | Background process with network capability. Background network activity is rarely legitimate in an agent context Run network commands in the foreground. If you need async work, explain why |
| `builtin-cron-persistence` | critical | block | Modifying scheduled tasks or system services creates persistent effects beyond this session Ask the user to configure cron jobs or system services manually |
| `builtin-cron-file-write` | critical | block | Writing to cron/systemd/launchd directories creates persistent scheduled tasks Ask the user to install services or cron jobs manually |

## Supply Chain

| Rule | Severity | Action | Description |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `builtin-rm-lockfile` | high | block | Deleting lock files breaks deterministic dependency resolution If you need to regenerate, delete the lock file and reinstall: rm <lockfile> && <install_command> |
| `builtin-lockfile-tamper` | critical | block | Lock files should only be modified by package managers, not by direct editing. Direct edits can introduce supply chain vulnerabilities Use the package manager (npm install, cargo update, etc.) to update dependencies |
| `builtin-npm-no-ignore-scripts` | medium | warn | Package install without --ignore-scripts. Lifecycle scripts (postinstall/preinstall) can execute arbitrary code from dependencies — this is the #1 npm supply chain attack vector (ref: axios@1.14.1 compromise, plain-crypto-js RAT dropper) Add --ignore-scripts to prevent malicious lifecycle scripts: npm install --ignore-scripts. If native modules need compilation (esbuild, sharp, bcrypt), run their build scripts explicitly after review |
| `builtin-build-script-injection` | high | warn | Package lifecycle script contains network/exec commands (possible supply chain injection) Review the lifecycle script carefully for malicious patterns |
| `builtin-npmrc-manipulation` | critical | block | Modifying package manager config can redirect dependency resolution to attacker-controlled registries (dependency confusion) If you need to change registry settings, ask the user to edit the file manually |
| `builtin-npm-publish` | high | warn | npm publish without --dry-run will publish to the registry. Accidental publishes can expose private code Use npm publish --dry-run first to preview, then ask the user to confirm the real publish |
